**Interpreting part design**

I need to output the JSON for a part that looks like a tapered lever or arm. It has a forked clevis on one end and a hook or cam on the other. From the images, the left end shows a clevis with a pin hole, while the right end has a rounded hook. Looking at the top view, the left end has a U-shaped fork, while the right end is rounded. It seems there's some confusion about orientation, but it looks symmetric overall, with a hole and a hook at either end.
**Analyzing clevis design**

In the isometric view, the clevis shows a hole near the left end, which is rounded with a through-hole or eye. Above this, there's a slot that creates two prongs. The right end looks like a hook with a semicircular cutout and a rectangular block at the end, possibly functioning as a latch. This part has 18 faces. Mapping the geometry, I find the bounding box ranges from -75.75 to 75.75 for length, 0 to 15 for thickness, and about 16.375 for width. The inner walls of the clevis slot seem to be at y=-3.5 and y=+3.5.
**Examining clevis holes**

I'm analyzing the surfaces of the clevis, focusing on faces 0 and 1, which show two cylinders with a radius of 3. Their axis is along the y-axis, implying these might be pin holes through the clevis ears. They are centered at x=-68.25 and z=7.5, with y at ±5.765. However, if the holes run along y, that would suggest a single cylinder instead. The two cylinders might actually represent the outer cylindrical surfaces of the rounded ears, possibly fillets or rounds on the corners.
**Identifying clevis prong shapes**

It looks like there are two symmetrical cylindrical patches on the left end, which likely represent the semicircular ends of each clevis prong, rather than holes. The faces 6 and 15 reveal larger cylinders with a radius of 7.5 and an axis along the y, positioned at x=-68.25 and y±5.864. This means the prongs have rounded outer ends extruded along the y-axis, creating semicircular profiles in the x-z plane. There are indeed two for each prong!
**Finalizing hook and clevis structure**

I'm working on defining the parts for the hook, starting with the outer cylinder and transitioning to a plane and inner notch. I need major_faces entries that include face codes and descriptions, so I'll assign them sequentially from FACE6 to FACE8. For the clevis, I'll use codes 0000-0006, the arm with 0007-0010, and the hook with 0011-0017, while ensuring the minor_faces section stays empty. The overall description will be “tapered clevis-to-hook lever link,” including various views. I'll establish relationships between sections to reflect their connections accurately.

part.name: Tapered clevis-to-hook link arm
part.description: Single solid link/lever with a forked clevis end (with two pin-boss ears and a central slot) transitioning into a long tapered arm body and terminating in a rounded hook/lug end with a concave notch and a rounded cap feature.
part.symmetry_note: Largely symmetric about the mid-plane y=0 (mirrored left/right across the slot and side faces), with end features split into mirrored pairs where the clevis slot interrupts cylindrical surfaces.

Section.name: Clevis / forked mounting end
features included: Forked clevis slot (U-shaped opening) at the end
Two clevis ears (upper/lower in width direction) with aligned pin-bore surfaces
Outer rounded end profile on each ear
Slot-bottom/end stop face inside clevis
Section.function intent: Provide a pinned mounting interface to a mating link/bracket while allowing rotation about the pin axis; transmit axial and bending loads from the pin into the arm body.
Section.physical behavior: Pin loads generate bearing pressure on the pin-bore cylindrical surfaces; the two ears act as parallel shear/bending members around the slot, while the rounded outer profiles reduce stress concentration at the clevis end. Loads flow from the bore region into the arm via the ear bodies and into the tapered web.
Section.geometry: End region split into two ears separated by a central slot; each ear has an outer cylindrical/rounded end surface (R7.5) and an interrupted pin-bore cylindrical surface (R3) due to the slot. The slot is bounded by two parallel planar inner walls and a planar end face (slot bottom) deeper into the part.
Section.location: At negative X extreme (x approximately -75.75 to -60.75), spanning full thickness z=0..15 and overall width y approximately -8.19..+8.19 with a slot between y=-3.5 and y=+3.5.

major_faces.name: Ear outer round (lower ear)
major_faces.description: Outer cylindrical surface (R7.5, axis along Y) forming the rounded end profile of one clevis ear.

major_faces.name: Ear outer round (upper ear)
major_faces.description: Outer cylindrical surface (R7.5, axis along Y) forming the rounded end profile of the mirrored clevis ear.

major_faces.name: Clevis slot inner wall (negative Y)
major_faces.description: Planar wall at y=-3.5 defining one side of the clevis slot opening.

major_faces.name: Clevis slot inner wall (positive Y)
major_faces.description: Planar wall at y=+3.5 defining the opposite side of the clevis slot opening.

major_faces.name: Pin-bore cylinder (upper ear segment)
major_faces.description: Cylindrical bearing surface (R3, axis along Y) for the pin bore in one ear; surface is interrupted by the slot, so only the ear segment exists.

major_faces.name: Pin-bore cylinder (lower ear segment)
major_faces.description: Cylindrical bearing surface (R3, axis along Y) for the pin bore in the mirrored ear; interrupted by the slot.

major_faces.name: Clevis slot end face (slot bottom/stop)
major_faces.description: Planar face at x=-60.75 that closes/terminates the clevis slot depth.

Section.name: Tapered arm web / main body
features included: Long tapered prismatic web between end interfaces
Opposed side faces with slight taper (in X-Y projection)
Top and bottom planar faces with slight slope (in X-Z projection)
Section.function intent: Provide the main load path between the clevis end and the hook end while minimizing mass via tapering; maintain stiffness and alignment between interfaces.
Section.physical behavior: Acts primarily as a beam in tension/compression and bending. The taper reduces cross-section toward one end, concentrating compliance where needed while keeping adequate stiffness near higher-load interface regions. Side faces and top/bottom planes provide global stiffness and define the arm envelope for clearance.
Section.geometry: Four dominant long planar faces forming a tapered prism: top plane, bottom plane, and two side planes (±Y). Planes are slightly angled relative to global axes, indicating taper and mild longitudinal slope.
Section.location: Central span along X between clevis region (around x=-60.75) and hook end region (around x=~60..75). Extends full thickness z=0..15 and near-full width y up to about ±8.19 with taper.

major_faces.name: Top face (tapered/slope plane)
major_faces.description: Large planar top surface spanning most of the arm length; slightly tilted (normal has small +X component).

major_faces.name: Side face (positive Y)
major_faces.description: Large planar side surface on +Y side; slightly angled due to width taper along X.

major_faces.name: Bottom face (tapered/slope plane)
major_faces.description: Large planar bottom surface spanning most of the arm; slightly tilted (normal has small +X component, opposite Z).

major_faces.name: Side face (negative Y)
major_faces.description: Large planar side surface on -Y side; slightly angled due to width taper along X.

Section.name: Hook / lug end interface
features included: Outer rounded end (large-radius cylindrical end surface)
Concave notch / hook seat (small-radius cylindrical surface)
Small side relief faces around notch (y=±3 planes)
Rounded cap/boss feature (cylinder with axis along Z)
Local end/top planar face at z=15
Section.function intent: Provide a receiving/engaging interface (hook/notch) for a mating pin/rod/edge and a robust end geometry for load introduction and retention; offer local clearance and contact surfaces for engagement.
Section.physical behavior: Contact occurs on the concave notch cylinder, generating compressive contact stress and tangential friction; the outer rounded end reduces snagging and stress concentrations. The end cap/boss and top face provide additional bearing/stop surfaces and strengthen the end against bending and prying loads.
Section.geometry: End region composed of a large outer cylindrical patch (R9, axis along Y), a smaller inner cylindrical notch (R3, axis along Y), a small additional cylindrical patch (R3, axis along Y) near the upper end, two small planar side faces at y=±3 that bound/relieve the notch area, a vertical-axis cylinder (R3, axis along Z) forming a rounded cap/side, and a planar top face at z=15 over part of the end.
Section.location: At positive X extreme (x approximately 59.75 to 75.75), centered around y=0, spanning thickness z=0..15 with local shaping near the end.

major_faces.name: Outer end round (main nose)
major_faces.description: Large cylindrical surface (R9, axis along Y) forming the outer rounded end of the hook/lug region.

major_faces.name: End top face
major_faces.description: Planar face at z=15 covering the top of the end region (local plateau/closure).

major_faces.name: End cap side cylinder (vertical axis)
major_faces.description: Cylindrical surface (R3, axis along Z) forming a rounded side/cap feature near the end.

major_faces.name: Hook seat / concave notch cylinder
major_faces.description: Concave cylindrical surface (R3, axis along Y) that forms the primary hook/notch contact seat.

major_faces.name: Notch side relief face (negative Y)
major_faces.description: Small planar face at y=-3 bounding the notch/relief opening on one side.

major_faces.name: Notch side relief face (positive Y)
major_faces.description: Small planar face at y=+3 bounding the notch/relief opening on the opposite side.

major_faces.name: Upper small cylinder patch near end
major_faces.description: Small cylindrical surface (R3, axis along Y) near the upper portion of the end shaping/transition.
